proof_summary: For the three small exponents, the congruence \(10^i\equiv1+9i\pmod M\) for \(M\mid81\), applied to a number and its reversal, forces \(M\) to divide its digit sum; the digit bound then gives the all-9s number as a lower bound, matching the divisibility-based upper bound. For every larger exponent, repeating the palindromic block \(29799999792\) exactly \(3^{n-5}\) times produces a shorter palindrome divisible by \(3^n\), since each tripling of the block repetition contributes another factor of \(3\), and hence gives a strictly smaller admissible value.
